concepts.name: Inertial reference frames
concepts.summary: Explain that an inertial frame is one moving at constant velocity without acceleration, and that observers describe events relative to such a frame.

concepts.name: Principle of relativity
concepts.summary: State that the laws of physics take the same form in every inertial frame, so no experiment reveals absolute rest.

concepts.name: Constancy of light speed
concepts.summary: Recall that light in vacuum has the same speed c for all inertial observers regardless of source or observer motion.

concepts.name: Events and spacetime coordinates
concepts.summary: Describe an event as a point specified by position and time in a given frame.

concepts.name: Failure of Galilean addition
concepts.summary: Understand why simply adding velocities contradicts the constant light speed and so must be replaced at high speeds.

concepts.name: Relativity of simultaneity idea
concepts.summary: Explain qualitatively that two events simultaneous in one frame need not be simultaneous in another moving frame.

misconceptions.text: Light's speed adds to the speed of its source, like a ball thrown from a moving train.
Relativity means that everything is relative and there are no absolute quantities.
Special relativity is only about observers who are moving, and a stationary observer sees the true physics.

concepts.name: Lorentz factor
concepts.summary: Calculate γ = 1/√(1−v²/c²) and judge how it grows as v approaches c.

concepts.name: Proper time
concepts.summary: Identify the proper time as the interval measured by a single clock present at both events.

concepts.name: Proper length
concepts.summary: Identify proper length as the length measured in the object's rest frame.

concepts.name: Length contraction formula
concepts.summary: Apply L = L0/γ to find the length along the motion measured in a frame where the object moves.

concepts.name: Light clock derivation
concepts.summary: Use a light bouncing between mirrors and the Pythagorean theorem to derive time dilation.

concepts.name: Time dilation formula
concepts.summary: Apply Δt = γΔt0 to compute elapsed time in a frame where a clock moves.

concepts.name: Muon decay evidence
concepts.summary: Explain how muons reaching Earth's surface confirm time dilation and length contraction.

misconceptions.text: Time dilation is an illusion caused by signal delay as light travels to the observer.
Lengths contract in all directions, including perpendicular to the motion.
The moving clock is the one whose own observer notices it running slow.

concepts.name: Lorentz transformation equations
concepts.summary: Apply x' = γ(x−vt) and t' = γ(t−vx/c²) to convert event coordinates between frames.

concepts.name: Relativistic velocity addition
concepts.summary: Use u' = (u−v)/(1−uv/c²) to combine velocities and show no result exceeds c.

concepts.name: Quantitative simultaneity and ordering
concepts.summary: Analyse how the term vx/c² makes spatially separated events non-simultaneous and when time order can differ.

concepts.name: Spacetime interval invariance
concepts.summary: Compute Δs² = c²Δt² − Δx² and use its invariance to classify intervals as timelike, spacelike or lightlike.

concepts.name: Spacetime diagrams
concepts.summary: Read and draw worldlines, light cones and tilted axes of a moving frame.

concepts.name: Causality and light cones
concepts.summary: Analyse why only spacelike-separated events can change order, preserving cause before effect.

concepts.name: Relativistic Doppler effect
concepts.summary: Calculate frequency shifts for sources moving relative to an observer using the relativistic formula.

misconceptions.text: Lorentz transformations can be applied to any two numbers like durations without regard to which events are measured.
Velocity addition just gives u+v unless speeds are very close to c.
Time order of any two events can be reversed by a suitable observer.

concepts.name: Four-vectors
concepts.summary: Represent events, velocity and momentum as four-vectors whose Minkowski norms are invariant under boosts.

concepts.name: Relativistic momentum and energy
concepts.summary: Use p = γmv and E = γmc² and analyse why they replace Newtonian forms.

concepts.name: Energy-momentum relation
concepts.summary: Apply E² = (pc)² + (mc²)² to systems including massless particles.

concepts.name: Mass-energy equivalence
concepts.summary: Evaluate binding energies and reaction Q-values by relating mass changes to energy released.

concepts.name: Invariant mass of systems
concepts.summary: Compute and justify the invariant mass of a multi-particle system, which is not the sum of the rest masses.

concepts.name: Relativistic collisions and decays
concepts.summary: Solve collision, decay and threshold problems using four-momentum conservation, choosing the most convenient frame.

concepts.name: Apparent paradoxes resolution
concepts.summary: Evaluate twin and ladder-barn paradoxes by identifying frame asymmetry and simultaneity differences.

misconceptions.text: Mass increases with speed, so relativistic mass is the real mass of a moving object.
E = mc² applies only to nuclear reactions.
Total mass of a system always equals the sum of its parts' masses.

concepts.name: Visual appearance of fast objects
concepts.summary: Evaluate how light-travel time and aberration make fast objects appear rotated rather than contracted.

concepts.name: Derivation from postulates
concepts.summary: Derive the Lorentz transformations from the postulates, homogeneity and isotropy, and design arguments for the invariant speed.

concepts.name: Lorentz group structure
concepts.summary: Evaluate how boosts and rotations form the Lorentz group, including rapidity addition and Thomas-Wigner rotation.

concepts.name: Covariant electromagnetism
concepts.summary: Judge how E and B mix under boosts and how the field tensor unifies Maxwell's equations as covariant.

concepts.name: Accelerated motion and Rindler frames
concepts.summary: Analyse worldlines under constant proper acceleration and the horizon seen by accelerated observers.

concepts.name: Lagrangian relativistic mechanics
concepts.summary: Construct a relativistic particle action and derive its equations of motion and conserved quantities.

concepts.name: Limits of special relativity
concepts.summary: Assess where special relativity fails in gravitational and quantum regimes and when it applies locally.

misconceptions.text: A fast-moving object would be photographed as visibly length-contracted.
Special relativity cannot handle accelerating objects or observers.
Electric and magnetic fields are separate entities, and their mixing under boosts is only a coordinate trick.
